description: Schema for extracting prospect/underwriting data from GHQ documents and emails - aligned with PricingPoint fields

location_name.description: Extract the company/location name from the PDF.

dba.description: Extract the DBA (Doing Business As) name from the PDF. If not available, return null.

first_name.description: Extract the first name of the company/benefit contact person. Look for contact information represented as Company Contact, Benefit Contact Name, Company Contact Name, or Benefit Contact. If the contact person's full name is available, split it into first name and last name.

last_name.description: Extract the last name of the company/benefit contact person. If a full name is provided, separate the surname/last name from the first name.

title.description: Extract the contact person's job title. If 'Title' is not available, use 'Decision Maker'. Only use 'Decision Maker' as the fallback value when the contact is clearly identified as the decision maker.

contact_type.description: Use the same value/rule as the title field. If the contact's title is available, use that title. If the title is not available and the fallback is Decision Maker, use Decision Maker.

email.description: Extract the contact email address. Extract the actual email address associated with the identified company/benefit contact.

cellphone.description: Extract the cellphone/mobile number only when explicitly available. Do not copy the regular phone number into this field unless the document explicitly identifies it as a cellphone/mobile number.

city.description: Extract the city. If 'City' is not separately provided, extract the city from the address field.

state.description: Extract the state. If 'State' is not separately provided, extract the state from the address field.

zipcode.description: Extract the ZIP/postal code. If not separately provided, extract it from the address field.

county.description: No extraction is required. Set this field to null.

aliases: Please identify all states of operation:
States of Operation (please check all that apply)
states_where_operating.description: Extract all states where the company currently operates. If checkboxes are provided, include ONLY the states whose checkboxes are selected/checked. Do not include unchecked states. If multiple states are selected, return all selected states. Do not assume that the state of incorporation is the only state of operation.

fed_tax_id.description: Extract the Federal Tax ID / FEIN from the PDF first. If not found in PDF, search email. Otherwise return null.

inferFromLocationName.condition: Only apply when corporation_type is not found or blank in the document
inferFromLocationName.note: Keywords are matched case-insensitively against location_name. If no keyword matches, fall back to default value.

corporation_type.description: Determine the corporation type from the location/company legal name (e.g. ABC Company LLC -> LLC, ABC Company Inc. -> INC). Extract legal entity type explicitly. If no recognizable entity type is present, use 'Others'. Do not invent a type.

naics_number.description: Extract the NAICS code from PDF, then email. Otherwise return null.

sic_number.description: Extract the SIC code from PDF, then email. Otherwise return null.

prospect_type.description: Extract the prospect type if explicitly provided in the PDF or email. If not available, return null. Do not infer the prospect type.

lead_source.description: Extract only from the email/mail when available. Use the value associated with the email. If not available, return null.

current_carrier_tpa.description: Extract the company's current PEO, payroll provider, or TPA information. Extract actual name. If both Yes/No question and provider name exist, use provider name.

additional_carrier.description: No extraction is required. Always set this field to NAN.

carrier.description: Extract the current medical insurance carrier from PDF, then email.

current_pr_peo_provider.description: Extract the current payroll/PEO provider information. Do not confuse medical carrier with payroll/PEO provider.

renewal_date_of_current_coverage.description: Extract the current coverage renewal date from PDF, then email.

requested_effective_date.description: Extract the requested/effective coverage start date. First search the PDF/GHQ. If not found in the PDF/GHQ, search the EMAIL for 'Benefits Effective Date' (e.g. 'Benefits Effective Date: October 1, 2026') and use that date.
conditions: If requested_effective_date is not available in the PDF/GHQ, extract it from the EMAIL using the label 'Benefits Effective Date'.
Convert the extracted date to YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 'October 1, 2026' becomes '2026-10-01').

payroll_frequency.description: Extract the payroll frequency/cycle (e.g. Weekly, Biweekly, Semi-Monthly, Monthly).

share_file_client_folder_link.description: Link to shared file or client folder

globalRules: Extract information primarily from the PDF/document.
If a field is not available in the PDF and the field allows email extraction, extract it from the email/mail content.
Search for the field using the listed labels, variations, and equivalent wording.
Do not hallucinate or infer information that is not supported by the PDF or email.
If a field has an explicitly defined default value below, use that default when the required information is not available.
If no value is available and no default is specified, return null.
Preserve the original value as much as possible, while cleaning obvious formatting issues such as extra spaces.
For checkbox-based fields, identify the options that are actually selected/checked. Do not include unchecked options.
When extracting names, separate the first name and last name from the identified contact person.
When both PDF and email contain the same field, prefer the PDF value, unless otherwise specified.
Never generate an email address from a person's name or invent a phone number.
Never assume a state is operating unless it is explicitly identified or selected.
If city, state, or ZIP code is missing as a separate field, extract it from the address when possible.
